findings.title: Nil TopicUser crash and bypassed TopicUser.change bookkeeping in unsubscribe
findings.body: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return `nil` if the user does not yet have a `TopicUser` row for the topic, causing `tu.notification_level` on line 107 to raise `NoMethodError` (500 error). Additionally, saving via `tu.save!` instead of `TopicUser.change` leaves `notifications_reason_id` and `notifications_changed_at` untouched (and skips publishing the change on `MessageBus`). When a `TopicUser` row was created by `UserNotifications#send_notification_email`, `notifications_reason_id` is `nil`; leaving it `nil` means `TopicUser.update_last_read` or `TopicUser.auto_track` will later automatically reset the user's notification level back to `tracking` when they view or post in the topic.

findings.title: Unsubscribe GET endpoint is non-idempotent and fails to stop emails for tracking users
findings.body:
`TopicsController#unsubscribe` mutates state on a `GET` request based on the current `notification_level`: if `> regular`, it sets `regular`; otherwise it sets `muted`. This causes two problems:
1. It is not idempotent: if a `watching` user reloads the page, clicks the email link a second time, or has the link prefetched by their email client/browser, the second request sees `regular` and downgrades the topic to `muted` (or overwrites a notification level the user just selected in the UI).
2. A user at `tracking` (the default after replying to or reading a topic) only receives emails when directly replied to, quoted, or `@mentioned`—the exact same email triggers as `regular`. Changing `tracking` to `regular` does not stop any email notifications for that topic despite the page stating "You will stop receiving notifications".

findings.title: Client-side transitions to topicUnsubscribe do not call the unsubscribe endpoint
findings.body: `TopicUnsubscribeRoute#model` calls `PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id)`. On a direct full-page load of `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe`, `loadTopicView` consumes the preloaded JSON produced by `TopicsController#unsubscribe`. However, if the route is entered via a client-side transition (when `topic_<id>` is not in `PreloadStore`), `PostStream.loadTopicView` requests `/t/:id.json` (`TopicsController#show`) rather than `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe.json`. The server never executes `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, so the user's notification level is not changed even though the UI states they have been unsubscribed.

findings.title: Overriding computed property details.notificationReasonText breaks when changing level
findings.body: `afterModel` hides the notification reason text by calling `topic.set("details.notificationReasonText", null)`. Because `notificationReasonText` is a computed property on `Discourse.TopicDetails` observing `notification_level` and `notifications_reason_id`, as soon as the user selects a new notification state in the `topic-notifications-button` dropdown on the unsubscribe page, the computed property recomputes and renders the reason paragraph inside the inline `.notification-options` container.

findings.title: add_unsubscribe_link without unsubscribe_url raises MissingInterpolationArgument
findings.body: `config/locales/server.en.yml` adds `%{unsubscribe_url}` to the `unsubscribe_link` translation, and `Email::MessageBuilder` interpolates `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` whenever `@opts[:add_unsubscribe_link]` is truthy (lines 67 and 90). However, `@template_args` does not define a default for `:unsubscribe_url` (unlike `:user_preferences_url`). Any caller constructing `Email::MessageBuilder` with `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without also passing `unsubscribe_url` will now raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument`.
